summary:
TrendSen is a browser-based detective game built on NASA data for Indonesia, covering hydroclimatic variables from 1980 to 2018. 
It tackle possible problem statement 'When students compare hydroclimatic variables across cities, it can be hard to tell whether an apparent rise or fall reflects a long-term trend or typical fluctuations across seasons and years.'
details:
“TrendSen” is a search-aid application to help observation of valid trends throughout each hydroclimatic variable. Specifically:

  • Aggregates Indonesia(South-East Asian Region) specific hydroclimatic variables from satellite data within the time range of 1980~2018.
  • Focus on influential hydroclimatic variables possibly in relation with hydrological calamity.
  • Rationalize abnormality of selected variables.
  • Visualise abnormal trends detected within the area of choice.
  • Centralizes information on a web platform to accelerate the process of inter-variable co-relation detection and possibly support user hypothesis.
Hydroclimatic variable - Sea surface height (SSH), 2 m air temperature, Land surface temperature, Precipitation, Near-surface humidity, Vapor pressure deficit (VPD), Evaporation rate.

How it works (refer to demonstration)

  1. Log in and pick a case. The player clicks the monitor in the office to open TD-OS, then chooses a case from CASES and reads its brief.
  2. Set up the investigation. In SETUP.EXE, the player chooses a variable, a place and a period within 1980 to 2018. Changing the setup after seeing results marks the case as exploratory.
  3. Lock a guess. Before seeing any data, the player guesses whether the trend will rise, fall, show no change, or whether they are not sure.
  4. Look at the record. PLOT.PCX shows the monthly series with its seasonal cycle, and no trend line yet.
  5. Run the lineup. LINEUP.EXE compares the trend with 1,000 trend-free simulations and runs the two trend tests, the multiple-testing correction and the robustness checks.
  6. Get a verdict. The case ends in one of three verdicts, with the reasons in plain words. The player’s guess is then marked as matched or not.
  7. Explore on MAP.EXE. The map shows each city or drawn circle with its own verdict, so the player can compare places.
Tools: Python with Flask, NumPy, SciPy and h5py for the statistics and API; Vite and Three.js for the front end; deployed on Vercel. The code is on GitHub at averagec/trend-detective.AI Tools used: Claude - helped write and debug the Python statistics, data-processing and API code, build the desktop game interface, draft and edit the documentation and submission text, and review the statistical tests for errors. The team reviewed Claude’s output before use.

What do you hope to achieve?

A trend line shows what changed. TrendSen gives you the conviction to find out why.
